units.title: Direct Sympatholytics and Nonselective α Blockers
units.sec: Direct Sympatholytics and Nonselective α Blockers · p63
units.guide: Anti-adrenergic drugs in this chapter are direct-acting sympatholytics, split first into α blockers and β blockers. α blockers are either nonselective α1+α2 blockers or selective α1/α2 blockers. Tolazoline is a small-vessel dilator for peripheral vascular disease/angiography, whereas IV phentolamine is the acute DOC for catecholamine excess situations such as cheese reaction, clonidine withdrawal and intraoperative pheochromocytoma hypertension.

units.title: Selective α2 Blockers and α1 Receptor Sites
units.sec: Selective α2 Blockers and α1 Receptor Sites · p63
units.guide: The α2 blockers here are yohimbine and idazoxan, with yohimbine noted as a food supplement for erectile dysfunction, neuropathic pain and postural hypotension. α1 blockers dilate vessels but their adverse effects depend on α1 subtype: α1a in prostatic urethra and iris gives ejaculation/floppy-iris problems, while α1b/d vascular blockade gives venodilation-driven first-dose postural hypotension and lowers LDL.

units.title: α1 Blocker Uses and Scorpion Bite
units.sec: α1 Blocker Uses and Scorpion Bite · p64
units.guide: Mixed α1a,b,d blockers such as prazosin, terazosin and doxazosin are used for BPH with hypertension and for scorpion bite. More selective α1a blockers, tamsulosin and silodosin, are BPH drugs, with tamsulosin also blocking α1d and silodosin having maximum side effects. Scorpion toxin has sympathetic and parasympathetic limbs: prazosin treats hypertension/pulmonary edema, atropine treats bradycardia, and severe priapism can need phentolamine.

units.title: β Blocker Classification by Selectivity, Generation and Vasodilation
units.sec: β Blocker Classification by Selectivity, Generation and Vasodilation · p65
units.guide: β blockers are organized by β1/β2 selectivity and by special vasodilator mechanisms. First-generation agents are nonselective, second-generation agents are β1-selective, and third-generation drugs may add vasodilation through α blockade, β2 agonism, calcium-channel block, nitric oxide or potassium-channel opening. Remember the named drugs carefully because the chapter tests exceptions such as nebivolol, carvedilol, labetalol and tilisolol.

units.title: Partial Agonism, Membrane Stabilisation and Water Solubility
units.sec: Partial Agonism, Membrane Stabilisation and Water Solubility · p65
units.guide: Some β blockers have intrinsic sympathomimetic/partial agonist activity; the mnemonic is 'Cause Partial Agonism' and pindolol has maximum action. This lowers bradycardia but makes these agents contraindicated after myocardial infarction and in migraine. Separate special groups include Na+ channel-blocking membrane stabilizers and water-soluble drugs that do not cross the BBB but are contraindicated in renal failure.

units.title: β Blocker Pharmacokinetic and Antioxidant Properties
units.sec: β Blocker Pharmacokinetic and Antioxidant Properties · p66
units.guide: The properties section gives high-yield extremes: nadolol has the longest half-life, esmolol the shortest because esterases metabolize it, carvedilol has maximum protein binding and celiprolol minimum protein binding. Esmolol is DOC intraoperatively and even for β blockade in asthmatics when necessary, while carvedilol and nebivolol are the antioxidant/cardioprotective examples.

units.title: β Blocker Adverse Effects: Brain, Bronchi, Glucose and Exercise
units.sec: β Blocker Adverse Effects: Brain, Bronchi, Glucose and Exercise · p66
units.guide: The side-effect mnemonic is 'BETA ONE in Heart, Kidney and metabolism.' Lipid-soluble β blockers cause central symptoms; bronchoconstriction makes asthma/COPD a contraindication; β blockade masks palpitations and tremors of hypoglycemia but not sweating; and β2 blockade causes exercise intolerance by reducing skeletal muscle contraction and blood glucose.

units.title: β Blocker Effects on Heart, Kidney and Metabolism
units.sec: β Blocker Effects on Heart, Kidney and Metabolism · p67
units.guide: At the organ level β blockers reduce contraction, heart rate, conduction and renin release. Their metabolic effects differ by generation/selectivity: nonselective agents worsen the lipid profile, cardioselective agents improve it in the table, and first/second generations increase insulin resistance while third-generation agents decrease it.

units.title: Clinical Uses of β Blockers and Toxicity Antidote
units.sec: Clinical Uses of β Blockers and Toxicity Antidote · p67
units.guide: β blockers are second-line antihypertensives overall, especially useful when renin is high or hypertension coexists with anxiety, migraine, tremor or hyperthyroidism. They are DOC in HOCM because lowering contraction reduces LV outflow obstruction, and they are used in aortic dissection, thyroid storm and glaucoma. Toxicity is treated with glucagon, which bypasses β blockade by stimulating adenylate cyclase and raising cAMP.
